# Further Reading {.unnumbered}

This book draws on three different kinds of source: R teaching, data architecture, and the official documentation of systems DataRaft can integrate with.

## Teaching R systems

*R for Data Science* is the main reference for progressive, workflow-first R teaching [@wickham2023r4ds].

*Tidy Modeling with R* is the model for teaching both a methodology and a family of cooperating R packages without turning the book into function-by-function documentation [@kuhn2022tmwr].

The Posit skills repository documents current R package development, testing, and Quarto authoring practices used while preparing this project [@positTesting; @positSkills].

## Architecture

*The Rise of Logical Data Management* motivates the broader architectural progression from physical integration toward a logical access and governance layer [@gardner2025logical]. DataRaft applies only a narrower R-first interpretation of that lesson.

For data mesh as an organizational and product-oriented architecture concept, see Dehghani [@dehghani2022datamesh].

## Interoperability and infrastructure

For contracts, see the Open Data Contract Standard project [@odcs].

For external lineage events, see OpenLineage [@openlineage]. For metadata catalog integration, see OpenMetadata [@openmetadata].

For the SQL transformation ecosystem that the experimental DataRaft bridge integrates with, see dbt documentation [@dbt].

For the local analytical database and lake technology used by `dataraft.lake`, see DuckDB and DuckLake documentation [@duckdb; @ducklake].

## DataRaft itself

For implementation details, prefer the current GitHub repositories and generated pkgdown references over this appendix. DataRaft is still a development package family, and experimental components may evolve faster than this book.

`AUDIT.md` records the exact source revisions used for this edition.
